title: Priority-windowed heartbeat + client-led reconnect protocol for partial-output reclamation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Long-running streaming generations often leave partial state on servers when clients disconnect or experience network partitions. Current GC heuristics aggressively evict after a fixed TTL which causes lost resumability for legitimate reconnects, or conversely retain partial state for too long and consume GPU memory under bursty traffic. This ticket proposes a hybrid protocol that combines a small priority-based heartbeat window, client-supplied reconnect hints, and progressive output pruning to reduce steady-state memory while preserving resumability for high-confidence reconnects. The protocol is intentionally client-led where possible (clients indicate intent to resume and provide a reconnect token) and server-governed via priority tiers and observability hooks. Goal: reduce unnecessary state retention by >=40% for medium-tail disconnects while keeping resume success rate >=95% for expected reconnect scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and SDK leads
Implementation gated behind runtime-flag and enabled by default in runtime-2.3 canary
Benchmarks show >=40% reduction in average in-flight partial-memory for disconnects with 1-10 minute reconnect distribution compared to current TTL baseline
Resume success rate >=95% for reconnects within the high-priority heartbeat window (configurable, default 2m)
No SLO regressions for p50/p95 latency under standard load profiles
End-to-end tests for client reconnect, soft-prune resume, and hard-GC recovery exist and pass in CI
design_decisions: Use a priority-windowed heartbeat: short, frequent heartbeats create a small high-confidence window (default 2 minutes). After window expires, state demotes to lower priority and becomes eligible for progressive pruning.

Client-led reconnect hints: SDKs will attach reconnect-intent tokens (signed) and optional last-delivered-offset to reconnection attempts; server verifies signature and uses token to rehydrate KV cache where available.
Progressive output pruning: prune older partial tokens first (prefix-preserving compaction) to reduce memory incrementally instead of full eviction; allows partial resumability at degraded fidelity.
Fallback policy: when memory pressure spikes, demoted state is compacted aggressively; implement fast-path cold fallback to a compatible smaller model variant to preserve latency SLOs.
Telemetry-first approach: expose metrics for heartbeat hit-rate, resume-to-fail ratio, memory reclaimed per-prune, and counts of client-led vs server-gc resurrections.
Security: reconnect tokens are short-lived and bound to session id + client fingerprint; server-side verification avoids accepting stale tokens. No PII in tokens.
tasks: Write design doc (confluence): protocol flows, data model, SDK contract, and config knobs
Prototype server-side priority window and demotion logic in streaming controller
Add reconnect token verification and session-binding logic
Implement progressive pruning compactor with prefix-preserving semantics
SDK changes: add reconnect token generation and automatic heartbeat behavior
Add metrics/traces and dashboard in Console for rollout monitoring
End-to-end integration tests: reconnect happy path, partial-resume degraded path, aggressive-GC path
Canary rollout: enable runtime-flag in canary region, monitor metrics for 48h
